summary: Expedition 73 compares 24 years of NASA temperature and precipitation records for the Colorado area and Northern Alaska. Explore temperature trends across 111 grid cells, rotate 3D terrain, and download the values behind the charts.
details:
Expedition 73 addresses the Be An Earth System Trend Detective! challenge through a browser app for comparing two fixed study windows, the Colorado area and Northern Alaska. A user selects 2 m air temperature or precipitation, views the annual time series, and reads the fitted change per decade and an approximate 95% confidence interval. The annual table and CSV expose the inputs to the fit. The globe locates the study windows.

The temperature trend map compares 111 grid cells on a shared scale for 2001–2024. Selecting a cell reveals its annual temperature series, fitted trend, and approximate 95% confidence interval. The rotatable 3D terrain uses NOAA ETOPO 2022 elevations and can display the same NASA temperature trends. The optional precipitation animation illustrates the selected month’s regional mean.

We use 288 NASA POWER monthly records per region and indicator from January 2001 through December 2024. The monthly regional means are combined into calendar-day-weighted annual means. We fit a linear trend and use Newey–West standard errors with two annual lags. For temperature, the fitted slopes are +0.29 °C per decade for the Colorado area and +0.41 °C per decade for Northern Alaska. The paired Colorado-minus-Alaska slope is −0.12 °C per decade. All three confidence intervals include zero. The regional precipitation estimates are −0.030 and +0.093 (mm/day) per decade, respectively, and both intervals include zero. The fitted signs describe this record, with uncertainty about the direction of the underlying trends. Northern Alaska lies above the latitude limit for MERRA-2 observation-based precipitation correction over land, so the precipitation estimates are interpreted separately.

Python validates and prepares the recorded data. JavaScript, HTML, and CSS power the interface. The public code and verification instructions are at https://github.com/sq0eezy/Expedition73
dataRefs: NASA Langley Research Center POWER Monthly API, sourced from NASA GMAO MERRA-2. T2M supplies 2 m air temperature and PRECTOTCORR supplies mean daily precipitation rates. These drive the regional comparisons and time-series analysis.
NASA GES DISC MERRA-2 M2C0NXASM v5.12.4 provides fractions for the temperature surface-weighting views.
NASA Earth Observatory Blue Marble provides the globe basemap.
NASA Scientific Visualization Studio Hurricane Arthur replay uses NASA/JAXA GPM data and is shown as a separate contextual example.
projectRefs: JAXA and NASA Global Precipitation Measurement mission, represented in NASA SVS’s Hurricane Arthur visualization.
MERRA-2 precipitation correction and high-latitude limits, NASA GMAO.
Newey and West, heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation consistent covariance estimation.
NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI), ETOPO 2022 Global Relief Model. Elevation data for the 3D terrain views of the Colorado area and Northern Alaska.
